instruction: Sort the data in the spreadsheet by the Discount column in ascending order (lowest to highest).

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting data by Discount in ascending order. Verified with Python that lowest discounts are 0 (rows with 'Manu LD' and 'Bellen'). Evaluator checks cells F2, F3 contain 0 and C2 contains 'Manu LD'.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Evaluator only checks 3 cells (F2, F3, C2) but does NOT verify that the entire dataset is sorted correctly by Discount column
Missing order verification: Does not check that all Discount values are in ascending order throughout the column (F2 <= F3 <= F4 <= ... <= Fn)
Weak logic: Checking only that F2=0 and F3=0 doesn't confirm proper sorting - multiple rows can have discount=0 in any order
No data integrity check: Does not verify that all rows are preserved and data integrity is maintained during sorting
Insufficient coverage: Instruction requires sorting ALL data, but evaluator only verifies top 2-3 rows - would pass even if middle/bottom rows are completely unsorted
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add comprehensive sorting verification: Check that Discount values are monotonically non-decreasing (F2 <= F3 <= F4 <= ... for all rows)
Verify multiple data points across the entire sorted range, not just the first 2-3 rows
Add checks for rows at the end of the dataset to ensure complete sorting (e.g., check that the last few rows have the highest discount values)
Consider checking a representative sample of cells throughout the sorted data (e.g., every 5th row) to ensure sorting is applied to the entire dataset
Add verification that the number of rows remains constant to ensure no data loss during sorting
